crosswalks.label: Video Game Designers
crosswalks.rationale: Video Game Designers directly ground gameplay/rule/design work, while this AXM profession is the narrower implementation-facing technical-design slice.

crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers ground implementation/tooling behavior but do not own game-design semantics.

findings.summary: Technical Game Design sits at the design-to-implementation boundary; successful scripts must preserve accepted rule semantics and cannot substitute for game-design/play evidence.
findings.rationale: Research-first compilation makes the profession boundary explicit before use.

gaps_against_body.description: Make implementation success, design-semantic authority and player/balance acceptance separate package-local evidence surfaces.

nonclaims: No complete Technical Game Designer reconstruction is claimed.
Occupational mappings are evidence, not profession identity.
No TEST/WORKING/CANON or adjacent authority is created.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: No adjacent professional, user, legal, platform or institutional authority is created.
